findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on an I/O Result panics on file-not-found, permission errors, or truncated reads
findings.failure_mode: external file path can abort the process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use ? to propagate the I/O error, or map_err into a domain error type

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on ParseIntError panics on non-numeric or out-of-range input for the second field
findings.failure_mode: a single malformed CSV line aborts the entire sensor load instead of returning a typed Parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u16>() with ? or map_err, and return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> or a domain error enum

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy `as` cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values >65535
findings.failure_mode: a sensor value of 70000 silently becomes 4436, corrupting data without any error signal
findings.fix: parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>() and use checked arithmetic or try_from for safe conversion

findings.problem: parts[0] — unchecked indexing into a Vec produced by split; if the line is empty or contains no comma, this panics with index out of bounds
findings.failure_mode: a blank line or a line without a comma causes a panic, not a typed error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on the Some/None variant, or use .get(0) with map_err

findings.problem: parts[1] — unchecked indexing; if the line has only one comma-separated field, this panics
findings.failure_mode: a line like 'sensor_name,' or 'sensor_name' panics instead of returning a Parse or MalformedData error
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and destructure the two fields explicitly; reject lines with fewer than 2 fields

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — I/O side effect inside the parsing/map logic that also does data construction
findings.failure_mode: the parser has hidden side effects, making it non-deterministic and untestable without capturing stdout; violates pure core principle
findings.fix: remove println from the core parsing path; log in the shell layer after parsing, or return parsed records and let the caller handle logging

findings.problem: load_sensors mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function — the functional core should be pure and the shell should handle all I/O
findings.failure_mode: the parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation; any change to file reading affects the parser tests
findings.fix: split into (a) a pure fn parse_records(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and (b) a shell fn load_sensors(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> that reads the file and delegates to the pure parser

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 — no domain newtypes, no validation at construction, no typestate for sensor lifecycle
findings.failure_mode: any code can construct Record with empty names, negative values, or invalid data; the illegal state of a Record with an empty name is representable
findings.fix: introduce newtype wrappers like SensorName(String) with a fallible constructor that rejects empty/whitespace, and validate value range at construction

findings.problem: Vec<String> = line.split(',').map(...).collect() — unbounded intermediate Vec allocation per line; no try_reserve, no capacity hint
findings.failure_mode: a single malformed line with many commas causes unbounded heap allocation; allocation failure is not handled
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to parse exactly two fields without collecting into a Vec; eliminates the intermediate allocation entirely

findings.problem: load_sensors returns Vec<Record> with no Result — all error paths use panic instead of typed errors
findings.failure_mode: consumers cannot distinguish between I/O failure, parse failure, and malformed data; all collapse into panic
findings.fix: change return type to Result<Vec<Record>, SensorError> where SensorError is an enum with variants like Io(io::Error), Parse(…) and MalformedLine(String)

findings.problem: println! is a visible I/O side effect that is not part of the function signature or return type — it is a hidden effect from the caller's perspective
findings.failure_mode: function behavior changes based on external console state; stdout capture may fail; non-deterministic in tests
findings.fix: remove println entirely from the data-loading path; push logging to the imperative shell layer

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_sensors — the function allocates per-line (Vec<String>, multiple String::to_string, clone)
findings.failure_mode: unknown allocation profile; per-line double-String overhead may be a performance bottleneck at scale
findings.fix: add a criterion or divan benchmark measuring allocations for a realistic CSV input; profile with flamegraph; consider &str-based parsing to eliminate per-line allocations

findings.problem: No [dev-dependencies] or [profile] sections — no benchmark framework, no test harness configured
findings.failure_mode: no way to run behavior tests or benchmarks for this crate; performance claims cannot be verified
findings.fix: add criterion or divan as dev-dependency and a [[bench]] section if benchmarks are required by the delivery contract

findings.problem: parts[0].clone() — unnecessary clone from already-owned String in the collected Vec
findings.failure_mode: wasted allocation per record; Record already owns the String so the clone is redundant
findings.fix: use parts[0].clone() only when needed; after refactoring to split_once, the owned string from split can be moved directly into Record

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sensors or any pure-parsing path
no profiler data (flamegraph, cargo-flamegraph, perf) for allocation profile
no allocation analysis (e.g., cargo-bench --benchmarks with --allocations) for the parsing loop
no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo test, cargo clippy were not executed in this review-only context
no second-ring analysis: no Miri, Kani, or loom evidence for unsafe or concurrent usage of Record
no command-layer evidence: no integration test showing end-to-end load_sensors with valid and malformed inputs
residual_risk: The crate has 10 blockers and 4 major findings: unwrap() on I/O and parse, lossy as cast, unchecked indexing, println! side effects, mixed I/O and parsing, no Result return type, no bounded allocation, and no benchmarks. Static review only; no commands executed. All blockers require source changes to reach Holzman compliance. Residual risk is HIGH — the code will panic on any malformed input, silently corrupt large values, and cannot be tested without stdout interference.
